entries.label: Nanomedicine
entries.quote: James Baker designs nanoparticles to guide drugs directly into cancer cells, which could lead to far safer treatments.
entries.note: Body text timings: "as little as five years"; "at least 10 years away".

entries.label: Epigenetics
entries.quote: Alexander Olek has developed tests to detect cancer early by measuring its subtle DNA changes.
entries.note: Body text timings: "by the end of this year"; "2008".

entries.label: Cognitive Radio
entries.quote: To avoid future wireless traffic jams, Heather "Haitao" Zheng is finding ways to exploit unused radio spectrum.

entries.label: Nuclear Reprogramming
entries.quote: Hoping to resolve the embryonic-stem-cell debate, Markus Grompe envisions a more ethical way to derive the cells.

entries.label: Diffusion Tensor Imaging
key_players: National Institute of Child Health and Human Development
entries.quote: Kelvin Lim is using a new brain-imaging method to understand schizophrenia.

entries.label: Universal Authentication
entries.quote: Leading the development of a privacy-protecting online ID system, Scott Cantor is hoping for a safer Internet.
entries.note: Body text timing: "in the next year or so".

entries.label: Nanobiomechanics
entries.quote: Measuring the tiny forces acting on cells, Subra Suresh believes, could produce fresh understanding of diseases.

entries.label: Pervasive Wireless
entries.quote: Can't all our wireless gadgets just get along? It's a question that Dipankar Raychaudhuri is trying to answer.
entries.note: Body text timing: "in just five years".

entries.label: Stretchable Silicon
entries.quote: By teaching silicon new tricks, John Rogers is reinventing the way we use electronics.
entries.note: Body text timing: "at least five years".

entries.label: Comparative Interactomics
entries.quote: By creating maps of the body's complex molecular interactions, Trey Ideker is providing new ways to find drugs.

notes: Ten entries, each framed around one researcher. Published March 2006. No availability field. Forward timings from body text are in entry notes. Read through a summarising fetch; medium confidence.
